source.title: OrthoEraser: Coupled-Neuron Orthogonal Projection for Concept Erasure
source.authors: Chuan-Cheng Shi; Wenhua Wu; Fei Shen; Xiaogang Zhu; Kun Hu; Zhi-Yong Wang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE feature units and neuron interventions as tools for concept erasure, and reports how those interventions affect generation. It does not test the claim versions about neuron interpretability rates, held-out explanation quality, or attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes concern erasure and generation quality after intervening on SAE features. The paper does not measure how many features have one or more jobs, test explanations on held-out activations, or evaluate attribution graphs. Other methods' results are comparators, not independent tests of the claim.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAE features in text-to-image models as a tool for concept erasure and reports only its own method's erasure and fidelity results. It does not audit how many neurons have one job, test explanations on held-out activations, score explanations by simulation, or build attribution graphs. It assumes polysemantic superposition and entanglement in dense activations without measuring their share.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SAE localization plus null-space projection onto coupled benign features gives a better safety–fidelity trade-off than prior erasure methods. They acknowledge dependence on SAE quality, the single-layer intervention and the fixed top-k selection. They frame dense activations as polysemantic and entangled, but do not measure this.
record.recipe_differences: This is a text-to-image concept-erasure method using SAEs, zero-ablation to find coupled features, and orthogonal projection; it is not an audit of neuron job counts or a held-out explanation-scoring procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with intervention layer; the paper also describes erasure and semantic-drift changes as λ varies, but gives no numeric outcomes for those settings in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: In SD1.4, suppressing the top ΔWFS SAE features cut I2P nudity detections from 646 to 5–17. Random features of equal number gave 598, and amplifying the selected features raised detections to 691. Similar reductions are reported in FLUX.1 Dev, AltDiffusion and Show-o2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In text-to-image models, a small set of SAE features selected by differential activation causally controls a harmful concept. These are SAE units, not native neurons, and the study reports no share of interpretable units.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. It states that the method depends on SAE dictionary capacity, resolution, and reconstruction fidelity; recognizes that the projection is a local linear approximation, uses one selected layer and fixed top-k coupled-feature selection, and may miss concepts not represented in the SAE. Cross-model detection results are reported as reductions without starting or ending counts in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the eight Table 1 body-part detection categories, the numerous baseline methods, or figure-only qualitative comparisons: these are concept-erasure outcomes or method comparisons, not tests of the claim versions. The text also gives no per-model CLIP-score changes for cross-model universality.

untested.parts: No neuron job-share audit in any language model, dense or mixture-of-experts.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic-neuron reanalysis.
No interpretable-neuron share across tools or architectures.
No attribution graphs and no comparison against a replacement model.
No held-out prediction test of explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Domain is text-to-image diffusion safety. The units are SAE features, not the model's own neurons. The paper's 'superposition' framing is assumed, not measured, so it bears on no version. The reported FID of 1.15 versus an unclear 16.64 reference is anomalous and should be treated cautiously.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or estimate of the share of neuron poles with one or more jobs or not understood.
No audit of language-model neurons across model scales or dense and mixture-of-experts architectures.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car analysis or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No measurement of interpretable-neuron shares across architectures or tools, and no InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.
No attribution graphs, reconstruction-error comparison, or test that such graphs explain behavior without a replacement model.
No test of explanations against activations not used to form them.
No automated explanation scoring by simulating activations on new text.
